items.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: back in 1932 I was about 15-1/2 and playing with a band at the Roseland Ballroom, Frank LaMarr and his stock arrangement orchestra

ctx.x: You know I look at your list of people you’ve played with, and I almost have to look at who you haven’t played with as opposed —

Yeah I think that makes more sense. When you talk about who I haven’t played with as a start, back in 1932 I was about 15-1/2 and playing with a band at the Roseland Ballroom, Frank LaMarr and his stock arrangement orchestra which drove me nuts. And that started it all off. Actually I was playing trumpet and then I substituted for a piano player and then just stayed at the piano, as opposed to playing second trumpet under an out of tune trumpet lead all night. And it doesn’t take long for one to get tuned into…
Speaking of out of tune, you must have encountered a few pianos along the way that were fairly out of tune.
